body.statement: At every \(P_0\in\mathcal M_I\), the common class \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\) is nonempty, and every estimator regular on \(\mathcal M_U\) has convolution variance at least \(V_U(P_0)=E_{P_{0,O}}[\phi_U^2]\). If \((a_x^U,d_x^U)\) solves \(\mathrm{QP}_x\) built from the profiled \(J\)-coordinate PT normals and the SC normals, then \(\phi_U=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}^{\prime}a_x^U\}=\sum_{x\in\mathcal X}\{g_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}^{\prime}d_x^U\}\), and \(V_U\) is the sum of the stratum program values weighted by \(p_X(x)\). This strictly strengthens SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, at intersection laws by replacing its two branch-specific asymptotic variances with the sharp convolution bound for estimators regular under PT-or-SC uncertainty.
body.justification: The theorem identifies the efficiency price of not knowing which nonnested identifying restriction is correct and makes that price computable by finite covariance algebra.
body.gap: SunXieZhang2025, Theorems 2--4, proves pointwise asymptotic and bootstrap laws separately under PT and SC; TchetgenTchetgenRobinsRotnitzky2010, Section 3, attains intersection efficiency for a different finite-support odds-ratio union, but provides no PT--SC restriction-normal program or ATT convolution bound.
body.consumer: RummoEtAl2026 can replace branch-contingent precision claims in its short-panel sugary-drink-tax comparison with the sharp variance envelope that remains valid when PT or synthetic comparison supplies identification.
body.proof_tex:
We first verify identification, keeping the causal target separate from the two observed-law functionals.  Under no anticipation, all observations before \(T\) equal untreated potential outcomes, and donor observations at \(T\) are untreated.  If PT holds, then for every \(x\) and every donor \(g\),
\[
 \delta_1^0(x)=\Delta\mu_g(x).
\]
Consequently the conditional treated effect is the treated observed final change minus \(J^{-1}\mathbf 1_J'D(x)\), and averaging with the treated-stratum weights \(p_X(x)p_1(x)/\pi_1\) proves \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_O)\).  If SC holds, full rank identifies \(w(x)\) from the preperiod equations and its final-period equation gives
\[
 E_F[Y_T(0)\mid G=1,X=x]=\sum_{g=2}^{J+1}w_g(x)\mu_{g,T}(x).
\]
Subtraction from the observed treated mean and the same treated-stratum averaging prove \(\theta(P)=\theta_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_O)\).  Thus the two observed functionals agree at every intersection law; neither equality is definitional.

For one stratum define
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)=g_{\mathrm{PT},x}+R_{\mathrm{PT},x}'a,
 \qquad
 \psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=g_{\mathrm{SC},x}+R_{\mathrm{SC},x}'d.
 \tag{1}
\]
The affine normal form in \(\mathrm{lem{:}tangent\text{-}normal\text{-}form}\) says that sums of the first functions in (1) exhaust the PT influence class, and sums of the second exhaust the SC influence class.  To see directly that their intersection is nonempty, note that \(r_{\mathrm{SC},x}=0\) and the intercept row of \(a=Bw\) imply \(\mathbf 1_J'w(x)=1\).  The PT normal span therefore permits replacing the uniform donor average in the PT gradient by the weights \(w(x)\).  Suppressing for one line the common treated-stratum factor \(p_X(x)p_1(x)/\pi_1\), call the resulting bracket
\[
 F_x=\mu_{1,T}-\mu_{1,T-1}-w'(\mu_{2,T}-\mu_{2,T-1},\ldots,
 \mu_{J+1,T}-\mu_{J+1,T-1})'.
\]
On the SC restriction set, the last preperiod matching equation is
\(\mu_{1,T-1}=w'(\mu_{2,T-1},\ldots,\mu_{J+1,T-1})'\), so \(F_x\) equals the SC final-level bracket there.  After restoring the common treated-stratum factor, the two stratum contributions agree; because their bracket difference is zero at \(P_0\), differentiation of that factor contributes zero to their derivative difference.  Hence the difference of their unrestricted derivatives annihilates the SC tangent space and, by the normal form, is an SC-normal linear combination.  The gradient of the weighted \(F_x\) contribution therefore has both representations in (1).  This supplies a feasible pair for every stratum and proves nonemptiness without presuming it.

By the definition of \(h_x\),
\[
 \psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)-\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d)=c(a,d)'h_x.
\]
Because \(\Omega_x=E_0[h_xh_x'\mid X=x]\) is positive semidefinite,
\[
 \Omega_x^{1/2}c(a,d)=0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 E_0[(c(a,d)'h_x)^2\mid X=x]=c(a,d)'\Omega_xc(a,d)=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Thus the constraint of \(\mathrm{QP}_x\) is exactly equality in \(L^2(P_{0,O}\mid X=x)\) of the two influence-function representations.  Its objective is
\[
 E_0[\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a)^2\mid X=x]
 =\ell_{\mathrm{PT}}(a)'\Omega_x\ell_{\mathrm{PT}}(a).
 \tag{3}
\]
Functions belonging to different strata have disjoint support and each stratum has positive mass by \(p_X(x)\ge\kappa_0>0\).  Therefore minimization of the unconditional squared norm separates over strata.  Equations (2)--(3) prove
\[
 \phi_U=\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{PT},x}(a_x^U)
       =\sum_x\psi_{\mathrm{SC},x}(d_x^U),
 \qquad
 V_U=\sum_xp_X(x)\min\mathrm{QP}_x.
 \tag{4}
\]
Singularity causes no ambiguity: all coefficient minimizers selected by the program represent the same minimum-norm function, and the Euclidean minimum-norm tie rule merely chooses coordinates.  The spectral-gap condition ensures stability of those retained coordinates but is not used to manufacture feasibility.

An estimator regular on the union is regular along every quadratic-mean differentiable submodel in each branch.  Its derivative covariance equations must therefore hold on both tangent spaces, so its regular influence component lies in \(\mathcal I_{\mathrm{PT}}(P_0)\cap\mathcal I_{\mathrm{SC}}(P_0)\).  Applying the convolution lower-bound result in \(\mathrm{lem{:}semiparametric\text{-}convolution\text{-}bound}\) and then (4) gives asymptotic variance at least \(\|\phi_U\|_{P_0}^2=V_U\).  The cited Sun--Xie--Zhang result \(\mathrm{lem{:}sun\text{-}xie\text{-}zhang\text{-}branchwise\text{-}laws}\) supplies separate PT and SC limit variances; (4) instead is the sharp lower bound imposed by regularity with respect to both branch tangent sets at an intersection law.  This proves the stated strengthening.
